title: Compute
description: A queue for long or heavy commands on the machine the tower runs on: each runs in the jobs daemon once the machine's named resources (lanes, a GPU…) have room for it, oldest first, and whoever queued it is told when it is over.

resources.description: What the machine has room for, in units of named resources, such as { "lanes": 4, "gpu": 1 }: a job starts only while the units it needs are free. Machine-wide: a floor's own value is not read.

defaultNeeds.description: What a job that says nothing of its needs holds while it runs.

queue.description: The machine's queue, oldest first: each job queued, started in the jobs daemon or refused by it, withdrawn before it started, and its requester told once it was over. Jobs are numbered from 1 in the order they were queued. Where a started job stands is the jobs log's, read from the board.

j.description: A job queued: its command, folder and label, the floor it was asked from, the resources it needs, the hours expected, its tags and the caps on them, a cleanup command, and who asked.

o.description: The scheduler started a queued job in the jobs daemon: `job` is the daemon's id for it.

f.description: The jobs daemon refused to start a queued job, and why.

q.description: A queued job taken out of the queue before it started, and by whom (a session, or `user`).

y.description: A job was over and its requester was told: what it was told (`outcome`), whom (`to`), why it couldn't be (`failed`), and how the job's cleanup command went.

run.description: Queue a command to run in the jobs daemon once the machine has room for what it needs, oldest first. It runs to its end outside your session and takes no input; you are told at your prompt when it is over. Its command is kept in the jobs log, which everyone reads: never put a secret or a result in it, and let the command read its own keys.

need.description: What it holds while it runs, as resource=units (lanes=2); the settings' defaultNeeds when left out.

hours.description: How long you expect it to run: the queue says when it runs past it.

tag.description: name=value words to group your jobs by (mission=boss-05-x): reads filter on them.

cap.description: tag=n: at most n jobs with this job's value of the tag run at once.

label.description: What it is, in a few words, as the queue and the jobs list show it; its command when left out.

cwd.description: The folder it runs in: absolute, or relative to your checkout; your checkout when left out.

cleanup.description: A shell command run in the job's folder once it is over, cancelled included, with COMPUTE_JOB set to its number: for what the job leaves outside itself (containers labelled with $COMPUTE_JOB).

cancel.description: Stop a job by its number: one still queued is withdrawn, one running is cancelled in the jobs daemon (SIGTERM to its process group, SIGKILL 5 s later) and its cleanup runs.

job.description: The job's number in the queue (#3 is 3).

jobs.description: The queue: the machine's resources in use, and each job queued, running, or over within the last day (every job with all=true), oldest first, with where it stands. tag=name=value keeps the jobs carrying that tag.

tag.description: name=value: only the jobs carrying it.

all.description: true: every job the queue holds, not only the last day's.

guidance.brief: Long or heavy runs: `tower x compute run --need lanes=2 -- <command>` queues one within the machine's resources and tells you when it's over; `tower x compute jobs` shows the queue.
guidance.full:
Compute queues long or heavy commands for the machine the tower runs on, so many workers on many floors share it without starting more than it holds.

- `tower x compute run [--need lanes=2] [--hours 3] [--label "plain words"] [--cwd <dir>] [--cleanup "<command>"] -- <command…>` queues one. It starts in the jobs daemon once the machine's resources (`tower x compute jobs` says them) have room for what it needs, oldest first, runs to its end outside your session, and outlives a tower restart. You are told at your prompt when it is over, with its exit: don't poll it from your turns.
- Its command is kept in the jobs log, which every worker reads: no secrets and no results in it or its label. Let the command read its keys from its own folder.
- Containers or other things it starts outside its own process group aren't stopped with it: label them with `$COMPUTE_JOB` (its number, set in its env) and pass `--cleanup` that removes only those.
- `tower x compute jobs` lists the queue and the running jobs with where each stands; `tower x compute cancel <n>` withdraws or stops one.
- `--tag name=value` groups your jobs (reads filter on it), and `--cap tag=n` keeps at most n jobs with that value running at once.
